about: feature 0004 T12: the negative jwt.validate and jwt.issue vectors in conformance/vectors/jwt/negative/, one vector per file (ADR 0045). Each entry's "file" member names its output file; it is not part of the vector and the split step below removes it.
regenerate: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const [src,dir]=process.argv.slice(1);for(const v of JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(src,"utf8")).vectors){const f=v.file;delete v.file;fs.writeFileSync(`${dir}/${f}.json`,JSON.stringify(v,null,2)+"\n")}' "$TMPDIR/negative-all.json" conformance/vectors/jwt/negative

Run both from the polyjose repository root. HS256 and EdDSA entries reproduce byte for byte; ES256 signatures and the JWE are randomized (gen.mjs README), so a rerun rewrites those files with other, equally valid bytes: regenerate only on purpose.

vectors.description: exp is the string "1300819380", not a JSON number, behind a valid HS256 signature. At now 1300819320 a parser that coerced it would accept the token (60 s before exp); a NumericDate MUST be a number: InvalidClaim (the CVE-2026-25537 class)
nbf is the string "0" (a coerced 0 would pass); exp is valid. A NumericDate MUST be a JSON number: InvalidClaim
iat is the string "0" and no max_age is set: iat is still type-checked (ADR 0027 §3), so InvalidClaim
exp is true, not a JSON number (a registered claim of the wrong type, null included): InvalidClaim
exp is null, not a JSON number (a registered claim of the wrong type, null included): InvalidClaim
exp is [1], not a JSON number (a registered claim of the wrong type, null included): InvalidClaim
exp is {}, not a JSON number (a registered claim of the wrong type, null included): InvalidClaim

exp is 9007199254740992 (2^53), one past the NumericDate range of ±(2^53 − 1); it would otherwise be far in the future and accepted. Written in the signed payload octets, since vector JSON stays within ±(2^53 − 1): InvalidClaim
exp is 1e300, finite but far outside ±(2^53 − 1); written in the signed payload octets: InvalidClaim
exp is -9007199254740992 (−2^53), one past the negative end of the range. In range it would be simply expired (TokenExpired); out of range it is InvalidClaim, which this pins
exp is 1e400, which overflows to a non-finite double; the JSON parser rejects non-finite numbers before claims are typed: InvalidJson
The Claims Set {"exp":1,"exp":2} names exp twice; polyjose rejects duplicate claim names (RFC 7519 §4 allows reject or last-wins) before any claim is checked: InvalidJson
The Claims Set {"exp":1,"\u0065xp":2}: the second name is exp after unescaping, so it is a duplicate: InvalidJson
The payload is the JSON array [], valid JSON but not a JSON object, so not a JWT Claims Set: InvalidJson
The payload octets are {"exp":1700000600,"name":"<0xFF>"}: the 0xFF octet is not UTF-8, so the Claims Set is not valid JSON text: InvalidJson
iss is the number 5, not a StringOrURI; no issuer is configured, so only the parse-time type check can reject it: InvalidClaim
aud is ["a", 1]: an array element that is not a string. The configured audience ["a"] would match the first element, so this pins the parse-time type check: InvalidClaim
aud is {}, neither a string nor an array of strings (audience ["a"] configured): InvalidClaim
No exp under the default policy: exp is required (ADR 0007) unless allow_missing_exp is set: InvalidClaim
exp 1700000600, now 1700000660 = exp + 60 with the default leeway 60: exp <= now − leeway, so the token is expired (the accepting side, now exp + 59, is a positive vector): TokenExpired
exp 1700000600 with leeway 0 and now exactly exp: the current time MUST be before exp, and it is not: TokenExpired
nbf 1700000100, now 1700000039 = nbf − 61 with the default leeway 60: nbf > now + leeway: TokenNotYetValid
max_age 300, iat 1700000061 = now + 61 with the default leeway 60: issued in the future beyond the leeway: InvalidClaim
max_age 300, iat 1699999639 = now − 361: older than now − max_age − leeway (1699999640): InvalidClaim
max_age 300 makes iat required, and the token has none: InvalidClaim
A leeway of 601 s is over the 600 s cap, so the policy is refused when it is built, before the (otherwise valid) token is looked at: InvalidClaim
iss is "https://A" and the accepted issuer is "https://a": StringOrURI values compare as exact, case-sensitive strings with no URI normalization: InvalidClaim
sub is "user-2" and the expected subject is "user-1": InvalidClaim
aud is ["x"] and the accepted audiences are ["api"]: no value matches: InvalidClaim
aud is [] with accepted audiences ["api"]: an empty array matches nothing: InvalidClaim
Accepted audiences ["api"] are configured and the token has no aud: aud is then required: InvalidClaim
aud is "api" and the policy names no audience (and does not set ignore_audience): the processor does not identify itself with a value in aud, so the JWT MUST be rejected: InvalidClaim
An at+jwt access token with iss, sub, aud, exp, iat and jti but no client_id, under profile access_token (issuer and audience configured and matching): client_id is required: InvalidClaim

An at+jwt access token with every RFC 9068 §2.2 claim valid but client_id null, under profile access_token (issuer and audience configured and matching), valid HS256 signature: client_id must be a JSON string (ADR 0052): InvalidClaim

An at+jwt access token with every RFC 9068 §2.2 claim valid but client_id a number (5), under profile access_token (issuer and audience configured and matching), valid HS256 signature: client_id must be a JSON string (ADR 0052): InvalidClaim

An at+jwt access token with every RFC 9068 §2.2 claim valid but client_id a boolean (true), under profile access_token (issuer and audience configured and matching), valid HS256 signature: client_id must be a JSON string (ADR 0052): InvalidClaim

An at+jwt access token with every RFC 9068 §2.2 claim valid but client_id an array (["a"]), under profile access_token (issuer and audience configured and matching), valid HS256 signature: client_id must be a JSON string (ADR 0052): InvalidClaim

An at+jwt access token with every RFC 9068 §2.2 claim valid but client_id an object ({}), under profile access_token (issuer and audience configured and matching), valid HS256 signature: client_id must be a JSON string (ADR 0052): InvalidClaim
An Unsecured JWT in the RFC 7519 §6.1 form (header {"alg":"none"}, empty signature) with valid claims, allow-list [HS256] and an HS256 key: never accepted: AlgorithmNotAllowed

An alg none token carrying a forged signature: the HMAC-SHA256 of its own signing input under the caller's HS256 key (computed with Python's hmac), so a verifier that ignored alg none and used the key's family would accept it. alg none is never accepted: AlgorithmNotAllowed
allowed_algs ["none"] with an alg none token: none can't be allowed, so the policy is refused: AlgorithmNotAllowed

Algorithm confusion: an HS256 token whose HMAC key is the SPKI PEM text of the RSA public key rsa-2048 (RFC 7520 §3.3), verified against a JWK Set holding that RSA public key with allow-list [RS256]: HS256 is not allowed: AlgorithmNotAllowed
The same algorithm-confusion token with allow-list [HS256, RS256]: HS256 needs an oct member and the set has only the RSA public key, so the RSA key is never used as an HMAC secret: NoMatchingKey
typ at+jwt under the default typing mode (absent or JWT only): an explicitly typed access token is kept out of generic validation: InvalidHeader
typ JWT under profile access_token, with every RFC 9068 §2.2 claim present and matching: the profile requires typ at+jwt: InvalidHeader
b64 false with crit ["b64"] and a validly signed unencoded payload: JSON Web Tokens MUST NOT use b64 with a false value: InvalidHeader
cty JWT on a signed JWT would mean JWS-in-JWS nesting, which is not supported: InvalidHeader
crit lists the extension urn:example:critical, which polyjose does not understand: UnknownCritical
A five-part compact JWE (dir, A128GCM, around a valid HS256 JWT) given to signed-JWT validation (no decrypt): the entry points are separate: InvalidFormat
A valid HS256 JWT rewrapped as a flattened JSON JWS (no unprotected header, signature unchanged): a JWT is compact only: InvalidFormat
The payload is swapped after signing (iss changed to https://attacker.example), keeping the signature: InvalidSignature
The protected header is swapped after signing for {"typ":"JWT","alg":"HS256"}: the same members in another order, so different octets under the signature: InvalidSignature
The low bit of the last signature octet is flipped: InvalidSignature
Header kid "z" against a set of members with kid a and b (signed by a's key): no member carries kid z: NoMatchingKey
Header kid "B", signed by the key of member kid "b": kid comparison is exact and case-sensitive: NoMatchingKey
The only member with kid a (the signing key) has use enc: not a signature key, so not a candidate: NoMatchingKey
The only member with kid a (the signing key) has key_ops ["sign"], without verify: not a candidate: NoMatchingKey
An EdDSA token and a set whose only member (the signing Ed25519 key) has JWK alg Ed25519: the JWK alg must be absent or equal the header alg exactly, and EdDSA ≠ Ed25519: NoMatchingKey
An HS256 token and a set whose only member (the signing 64-octet oct key) has JWK alg HS512: bound to another algorithm, so not a candidate: NoMatchingKey

A kid-less ES256 token and a set of nine kid-less P-256 members (the first is the signing key): nine candidates exceed the default max_key_candidates 8, refused before any signature is computed: NoMatchingKey
A kid-less ES256 token signed by p256-cand-9 and a set of three other kid-less P-256 members: every candidate is tried and fails, ranked: InvalidSignature

The RFC 7515 A.2 RS256 token against a set whose only member is a three-prime RSA private key (oth with one r/d/t entry; the OpenSSL 4.1.0 key fixture reject-rsa2048-3prime-private-pkcs8.pem, its members from openssl pkey -text): multi-prime keys are unsupported (ADR 0067 §3), so the member is skipped at import (RFC 7517 §5) instead of failing the set, and no candidate is left: NoMatchingKey

The header embeds the attacker's public key as jwk, with kid "attacker", and is signed by that key; the real set holds kid a and b. Embedded keys never supply keys, and kid attacker selects no member: NoMatchingKey
The header embeds the attacker's public key as jwk and copies the real kid "a"; it is signed by the attacker's key. Member a is selected and the embedded key ignored: InvalidSignature
The header embeds the attacker's public key as jwk with no kid, signed by that key: both real members are candidates and neither verifies; the embedded key is never tried: InvalidSignature

The RFC 7515 A.2 RS256 token, allow-list [RS256], against a set whose only RS256-capable member is an 8200-bit RSA public key (over the 8192-bit import limit, so skipped at import) next to a P-256 key: no candidate remains: NoMatchingKey

A valid HS256 JWT (protected header {"alg":"HS256"}) rewrapped as flattened JSON with the attacker unprotected header {"typ":"at+jwt"}; protected header and signature unchanged, so the signature is valid. A JWT is compact only (ADR 0027 §6), and typing is never read from an unprotected header (ADR 0049 §2): InvalidFormat under the default policy

A valid HS256 JWT with every RFC 9068 §2.2 claim but no protected typ, rewrapped as flattened JSON with the attacker unprotected header {"typ":"at+jwt"} to pass as an access token; signature unchanged and valid. A JWT is compact only (ADR 0027 §6), and typing is never read from an unprotected header (ADR 0049 §2): InvalidFormat under profile access_token
The payload is swapped after signing and both payloads are expired at now (exp + 3600): claims are parsed only after the signature verifies (step 9 before J5): InvalidSignature
An HS256 token with typ at+jwt under the default typing mode and allow-list [HS384]: the allow-list (step 7) comes before the JWT header rules (J1): AlgorithmNotAllowed
An ES256 token with typ at+jwt (default typing mode) and kid "z" unknown to the set: the JWT header rules (J1) come before key selection (J2): InvalidHeader
An ES256 token with kid "z" unknown to the set, expired at now (exp + 3600): key selection (J2) comes before the claims (J5): NoMatchingKey
aud "other" against accepted audiences ["api"], and expired at now (exp + 3600): exp (J5) comes before aud (J10): TokenExpired

No exp under the default policy and iss https://attacker.example against the accepted issuer https://issuer.example: required-claim presence (J4) comes before the iss check (J8); both give InvalidClaim

Issuing RS256 with the RSA public key rsa-2048 (RFC 7520 §3.3): RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 signing needs the private key (RFC 8017 §8), so a public key is never a signing key: KeyAlgorithmMismatch (ADR 0026 §2 step 8, ADR 0067 §2)

Issuing PS256 with the RSA public key rsa-2048 (RFC 7520 §3.3): RSASSA-PSS signing needs the private key (RFC 8017 §8), so a public key is never a signing key: KeyAlgorithmMismatch (ADR 0026 §2 step 8, ADR 0067 §2)
Issuing with alg none (an Unsecured JWT) and an oct key: never produced: AlgorithmNotAllowed
Issuing ES256 with a P-384 private key: ES256 is bound to P-256: KeyAlgorithmMismatch
